Q1: Chloromethane exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive toxicity (CMR), oral toxicity (ORL), and organ/systemic toxicity (OGN). It also has an expanded hazard profile (Tier 2) for inhalation, and is considered a low/moderate environmental hazard (Tier 3). Data gaps (Tier 4) currently exist for endocrine disruption and dermal/eye hazards.
Q2: Chloromethane is identified on several prominent "Lists of Concern," including California's Proposition 65 due to its known potential to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. It is also regulated by the EPA, appearing on their Drinking Water Standard list and designated as a Hazardous Air Pollutant.
Q3: Chloromethane is generally well-characterized, evidenced by a substantial body of scientific literature with 17,000 references, a clearly defined molecular formula (CH3Cl), and classification as a "Small Molecule." While two hazard categories (endocrine disruption and dermal/eye hazards) are currently data deficient (Tier 4), the overall robust data availability suggests a relatively comprehensive understanding of its properties.
